Where You Are: The Planning Step, What Came Before It and Who Is Involved After It

The nine steps of the Medicaid Planning Roadmap, with yours marked.

Download PDF

When Mom needs long-term care now, you hear about applications, attorneys and paperwork all at once, and it can sound as if every part of it belongs to this week. There is a general order to it, and it helps to see it laid out as steps, with the one you're on marked.

This page shows the whole road, where the planning step sits on it, what it produces, and who is involved next.

Phase 1 · Assess

Understand where you are today.

  1. 1

    Understand Care Needs → Levels of Care & Costs → Care Plan

    You finish with: Immediate Care Needs Assessment

  2. 2

    Organize Income & Assets → Ownership & Expenses → Financial File

    You finish with: Financial Snapshot & Care Cost Analysis

  3. 3

    Assess Care & Nonfinancial Eligibility → Income & Assets → Barriers & Readiness

    You finish with: Medicaid Readiness Assessment

Phase 2 · Plan

Develop and implement your strategy.

  1. 4

    Plan Barriers & Issues → Priorities & Professional Team → Written Plan

    You finish with: Medicaid Action Plan

    You are here. This step turns what you know about Mom's care, her finances and where things stand with Medicaid into a written plan. It moves from barriers and open issues, to priorities and the professional team, to the plan on paper. It is finished when everyone can answer what happens next, who is responsible, and in what order things need to happen.

  2. 5

    Legal Authority & Documents → Property, Trusts & Transfers → Attorney Review

    You finish with: Legal Issues & Attorney Review Brief

  3. 6

    Financial Costs & Runway → Asset Treatment & Tools → Strategy & Documentation

    You finish with: Financial Strategy & Implementation Plan

Phase 3 · Secure

Secure benefits, protect assets, and maintain eligibility.

  1. 7

    Apply Prepare → Submit → Manage

    You finish with: Medicaid Application File

  2. 8

    Protect What May Be Protected → What May Remain Exposed → What Needs Ongoing Attention

    You finish with: Asset Protection Report

  3. 9

    Maintain Ongoing Requirements → Changes & Renewals → Maintenance System

    You finish with: Medicaid Maintenance Plan

What came before it

Three steps come before this one: understanding Mom's care needs, organizing her finances, and assessing where things stand with Medicaid. Each leaves something on paper, and the plan is built from all three.

If your family arrived at this step first because Mom needs care now, the planning conversation can start from a short summary of each, with the gaps marked as questions.

What this step produces

The Medicaid Action Plan: a written, prioritized plan of what needs to happen, in what order, and who is responsible for each part. It is worked out with your Medicaid planner from Mom's facts.

It is a plan, not a decision about eligibility. The federal Administration for Community Living explains that each state takes the applications and makes the eligibility determinations, and that eligibility rules vary from state to state.12

What happens next

Two steps carry the plan out: the legal step and the financial step. After them come Apply, Protect and Maintain. The roadmap shows them in a general order. Which of them your family needs, and in what order for Mom, is what the plan itself says.

An elder law attorney reviews parts of the plan in this step and does the work of the legal step. The Administration for Community Living lists preparing power of attorney documents and exploring a person's qualifications for Medicaid among the things elder law attorneys do.3

Who is involved, by role

  • You and your family: gathering, writing down, asking, and making the decisions that are yours to make.
  • Mom: her own wishes, as far as she can share them.
  • Your Medicaid planner: brings the care, financial and Medicaid findings together, names the known barriers and open issues, and works with the family to separate what must happen now from what can wait and to put the actions in order, with a name beside each one.
  • An elder law attorney: reviews the decisions that belong to an attorney before the written plan is settled. Legal advice and legal documents are the attorney's, in the step that follows.
  • A licensed financial or insurance professional: reviews the financial and insurance decisions that belong to them before the plan is settled.
  • An applications specialist and the state Medicaid agency: the application is prepared with a specialist, and the state makes the decision. That is step seven.

What this page doesn't promise

How long any step takes, who will be available, or how things turn out. It doesn't put your family's own actions in order, and nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice. Families move through the steps at different speeds.
